clues: A town on a plain in Turkey is ringed by tall mountains. High peaks stand to its north, west, and south.
Winters here are cold and snowy, while summers are mostly cool. Yet this place stays five to six degrees warmer than Erzurum.
Its Ulu Cami Mosque was built in 1734 by Alaeddin, the bey of Muş. An old castle also stands in the town today.
Its flat land is one of the most fertile plains in the region. Farms and herds, not shops or factories, earn most people their living.
This town sits close to Hamurpert Lake. That lake holds a big place in local history.
